# Platform CLI commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from `origin --help` of the release scripts/origin-cli.version pins (v1.19.0).
     Do not edit by hand: fix the help text in origincloudhq/cli, or scripts/cli_reference_overrides.yml, and rerun. -->

This page lists the options every `origin` command accepts, and every `origin id`, `origin config`, `origin resourcemanager`, `origin location`, `origin billing`, `origin support` and `origin mcp` command. For installing and configuring the CLI, see [Use the CLI](../access/cli.md).

## Global options

Every `origin` command accepts these options. Give `--config` and `--api` before the command group, such as `origin --config <file> pvs list-volumes`; `--output` goes anywhere.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-c`, `--config <FILE>` | Path of the CLI configuration file to use instead of the default one. |
| `-a`, `--api <URL>` | GraphQL API endpoint `origin id login` reads the signed-in user from, which applies their pending invitations. Default: `https://graph.origincloudapis.eu/graphql`. |
| `-o`, `--output <FORMAT>` | Output format. Overrides ORIGINCLOUD_OUTPUT_FORMAT and the profile's `output-format`; without any of them, `table` on a terminal and `json` when the output goes to a pipe or a file. Possible values: - table: A list as a table, a resource as its fields, one per line - wide: A list as a table of every field that fits in a cell - json: The response as the API sends it, in JSON - name: The resource names alone, one per line. |
| `--color <WHEN>` | When the `table`, `wide` and `name` formats use colour: `auto` on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set. Possible values: - auto: On a terminal, unless `NO_COLOR` is set (`CLICOLOR_FORCE` forces it) - always: Always, through a pipe too - never: Never. Default: `auto`. |
| `--no-pager` | Print `table` and `wide` output taller than the terminal as it is, instead of through ORIGINCLOUD_PAGER, PAGER or `less`. |

`origin --version` prints the CLI's version. `origin --help`, `origin <group> --help` and `origin <group> <command> --help` print the help this page is generated from.

## origin completion

Complete `origin`'s commands, flags and their values in your shell: run it on a terminal to see how to install it. On a terminal, it says how to install the completion in the shell (or SHELL's, when none is named); into a file or a pipe, it prints the script itself, for `> file` or `eval "$(origin completion bash)"`.

```sh
origin completion [OPTIONS] [SHELL]
```

## origin version

Print version and exit.

```sh
origin version [OPTIONS]
```

## origin id

Authenticate with Origin Cloud Identity.

### login

Log in through your browser, with a code on another device, or as a service account with your identity provider's token. Opens the Origin Cloud login page in your browser and waits for you to log in there. With --device, prints an address and a code to approve on any other device instead, for machines without a browser such as an SSH session. The CLI never asks for your password. With --oidc-token-file, assumes a `WORKLOAD` service account with a token from your own identity provider, which one of the account's federated credentials trusts, and runs the commands that follow as that account. Once its access token expires, the CLI reads the file again and assumes the account again, so a file the identity provider or a credential helper keeps current keeps the login going; a token from standard input (`-`) is read once.

```sh
origin id login [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--device` | no | Log in by approving a code on another device, instead of opening a browser on this machine. |
| `--oidc-token-file <PATH>` | no | Log in as a service account with the identity provider's token in this file, or on standard input with `-`. |
| `--service-account <NAME>` | no | The service account to assume with --oidc-token-file, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`; without it, the one whose federated credential trusts the token. |

### token

Print the access token of the current login session, for calling the API directly. Without a login session, on an instance that runs as a service account, the credential of that service account.

```sh
origin id token [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-a`, `--as-header` | no | Print the token as an HTTP `Authorization` header (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). |
| `-r`, `--raw` | no | Print plain text with no JSON envelope, for direct use in shell one-liners (e.g. `curl -H "$(origin id token --as-header --raw)"`). |

## origin config

Cli configuration.

### profile

Show the values stored in the local CLI profile.

```sh
origin config profile [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### profile-set

Set a value in the local CLI profile. Keys: `default-username` (prefilled at `origin id login`), `output-format` (`table`, `wide`, `json` or `name`; without it, `table` on a terminal and `json` otherwise), `default-project` and `default-zone` (used by the generated commands, such as `origin pvs`, when `--project` or `--zone` isn't given) and `region` (the region they work in: their `--region` when not given, and the front door of the services with regional hosts, such as `pvs`; without it, the region of `default-zone`). `origin config profile-set region eu-central1` sets the region. The environment variables ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT, ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE and ORIGINCLOUD_REGION override the profile's values, and a flag overrides both.

```sh
origin config profile-set [OPTIONS] <KEY> <VALUE>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<KEY>` | The key to set. |
| `<VALUE>` | Its value. |

## origin resourcemanager

Resource manager: organizations and projects, and their quotas.

Every `origin resourcemanager` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host, `https://resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu`, the same in every region. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_RESOURCEMANAGER_ENDPOINT`. |

### get-organization

Returns an organization.

```sh
origin resourcemanager get-organization [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization to return. Its id, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}`. |

### list-organizations

Lists the organizations the caller holds a role in, oldest first.

```sh
origin resourcemanager list-organizations [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most organizations to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### create-organization

Creates an organization. Any signed-in user can create one, and becomes its owner and the administrator of its default billing account, which is created with it without billing details: the organization can't be invoiced until they are set with the billing API (`billing.origincloudapis.eu`). A new organization is either `ACTIVE` at once or `PENDING_REVIEW`, depending on the platform's free capacity.

```sh
origin resourcemanager create-organization [OPTIONS] --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>` | yes | The name the console shows, typically the company's name. Not empty. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the organization the first request created instead of creating a second one. One is generated when not given. |

### update-organization

Renames an organization.

```sh
origin resourcemanager update-organization [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> <--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization to change. Its id, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}`. |
| `--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>` | yes | The name the console shows, typically the company's name. Not empty. Left as it is when not given. |

### delete-organization

Deletes an organization. Refused as a `CONFLICT` while it still has a project, or a service account that isn't deleted, which the error names: delete them first. Nothing is deleted then. Its quota, its pending invitations and every role granted in it go with it. Its billing accounts stay, with their spend limits, so the last period can still be invoiced.

```sh
origin resourcemanager delete-organization [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization to delete. Its id, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}`. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-organization-quota

Returns an organization's quota: the most of each kind of resource its projects may hold together, and how much of it they use. The limits are set by the platform; ask support to raise one.

```sh
origin resourcemanager get-organization-quota [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The quota to return, `organizations/{organization}/quota`. Its id, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/quota`. |

### get-project

Returns a project.

```sh
origin resourcemanager get-project [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | yes | The project to return. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}`. |

### list-projects

Lists an organization's projects, oldest first.

```sh
origin resourcemanager list-projects [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization whose projects to list, `organizations/{organization}`. Its id, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}`. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most projects to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### create-project

Creates a project in an `ACTIVE` organization, under the id the caller chooses. The caller becomes the project's owner, and the project is billed to the organization's default billing account. An id in use, or used by a project that was deleted, is refused as a `CONFLICT`.

```sh
origin resourcemanager create-project [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME> --project-id <PROJECT_ID>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization the project belongs to, `organizations/{organization}`. Its id, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}`. |
| `--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>` | yes | The name the console shows. Not empty. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the project the first request created instead of creating a second one. One is generated when not given. |
| `--project-id <PROJECT_ID>` | yes | The project's id, the last segment of its name: 6 to 16 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen, such as `acme-prod`. |

### update-project

Renames a project.

```sh
origin resourcemanager update-project [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT> <--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | yes | The project to change. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}`. |
| `--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>` | yes | The name the console shows. Not empty. Left as it is when not given. |

### delete-project

Deletes a project. Refused as a `CONFLICT` while the project still has a resource you can delete yourself: an instance that isn't terminated, an image, a key pair, a volume or snapshot that isn't deleted, a NAT gateway, a floating IP, a VPC, or a DNS policy other than its default one. The refusal names every kind left, in the order to delete them. Nothing you can delete yourself is deleted on your behalf. The project's default DNS policy, its quota and every role granted on it go with it; roles granted on the organization stay.

```sh
origin resourcemanager delete-project [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | yes | The project to delete. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}`. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-project-quota

Returns a project's quota: the budget of each kind of resource the project may hold, if one is set, and how much of it the project uses.

```sh
origin resourcemanager get-project-quota [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | yes | The quota to return, `projects/{project}/quota`. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/quota`. |

### update-project-quota

Sets or removes a project's budgets. A budget named in `updateMask` is set to the value given, or removed when the value is left out.

```sh
origin resourcemanager update-project-quota [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT> <--max-instances <MAX_INSTANCES>|--no-max-instances|--max-vcpu <MAX_VCPU>|--no-max-vcpu|--max-volume-gib <MAX_VOLUME_GIB>|--no-max-volume-gib|--max-vpcs <MAX_VPCS>|--no-max-vpcs|--max-public-ips <MAX_PUBLIC_IPS>|--no-max-public-ips|--max-hosted-zones <MAX_HOSTED_ZONES>|--no-max-hosted-zones|--max-record-sets <MAX_RECORD_SETS>|--no-max-record-sets>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | yes | The project quota to change. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/quota`. |
| `--max-instances <MAX_INSTANCES>` | one of `--max-instances`, `--no-max-instances`, `--max-vcpu`, `--no-max-vcpu`, `--max-volume-gib`, `--no-max-volume-gib`, `--max-vpcs`, `--no-max-vpcs`, `--max-public-ips`, `--no-max-public-ips`, `--max-hosted-zones`, `--no-max-hosted-zones`, `--max-record-sets`, `--no-max-record-sets` | The most instances that aren't terminated; unset means no budget. Each budget is zero or more, and no more than the organization's limit for the same kind. Left as it is when not given. `--no-max-instances` unsets it. |
| `--no-max-instances` | one of `--max-instances`, `--no-max-instances`, `--max-vcpu`, `--no-max-vcpu`, `--max-volume-gib`, `--no-max-volume-gib`, `--max-vpcs`, `--no-max-vpcs`, `--max-public-ips`, `--no-max-public-ips`, `--max-hosted-zones`, `--no-max-hosted-zones`, `--max-record-sets`, `--no-max-record-sets` | Unsets `--max-instances`; the API's default applies. |
| `--max-vcpu <MAX_VCPU>` | one of `--max-instances`, `--no-max-instances`, `--max-vcpu`, `--no-max-vcpu`, `--max-volume-gib`, `--no-max-volume-gib`, `--max-vpcs`, `--no-max-vpcs`, `--max-public-ips`, `--no-max-public-ips`, `--max-hosted-zones`, `--no-max-hosted-zones`, `--max-record-sets`, `--no-max-record-sets` | The most vCPUs, summed over the instances that aren't terminated; unset means no budget. Left as it is when not given. `--no-max-vcpu` unsets it. |
| `--no-max-vcpu` | one of `--max-instances`, `--no-max-instances`, `--max-vcpu`, `--no-max-vcpu`, `--max-volume-gib`, `--no-max-volume-gib`, `--max-vpcs`, `--no-max-vpcs`, `--max-public-ips`, `--no-max-public-ips`, `--max-hosted-zones`, `--no-max-hosted-zones`, `--max-record-sets`, `--no-max-record-sets` | Unsets `--max-vcpu`; the API's default applies. |
| `--max-volume-gib <MAX_VOLUME_GIB>` | one of `--max-instances`, `--no-max-instances`, `--max-vcpu`, `--no-max-vcpu`, `--max-volume-gib`, `--no-max-volume-gib`, `--max-vpcs`, `--no-max-vpcs`, `--max-public-ips`, `--no-max-public-ips`, `--max-hosted-zones`, `--no-max-hosted-zones`, `--max-record-sets`, `--no-max-record-sets` | The most GiB of volumes that aren't deleted; unset means no budget. Left as it is when not given. `--no-max-volume-gib` unsets it. |
| `--no-max-volume-gib` | one of `--max-instances`, `--no-max-instances`, `--max-vcpu`, `--no-max-vcpu`, `--max-volume-gib`, `--no-max-volume-gib`, `--max-vpcs`, `--no-max-vpcs`, `--max-public-ips`, `--no-max-public-ips`, `--max-hosted-zones`, `--no-max-hosted-zones`, `--max-record-sets`, `--no-max-record-sets` | Unsets `--max-volume-gib`; the API's default applies. |
| `--max-vpcs <MAX_VPCS>` | one of `--max-instances`, `--no-max-instances`, `--max-vcpu`, `--no-max-vcpu`, `--max-volume-gib`, `--no-max-volume-gib`, `--max-vpcs`, `--no-max-vpcs`, `--max-public-ips`, `--no-max-public-ips`, `--max-hosted-zones`, `--no-max-hosted-zones`, `--max-record-sets`, `--no-max-record-sets` | The most VPCs; unset means no budget. Left as it is when not given. `--no-max-vpcs` unsets it. |
| `--no-max-vpcs` | one of `--max-instances`, `--no-max-instances`, `--max-vcpu`, `--no-max-vcpu`, `--max-volume-gib`, `--no-max-volume-gib`, `--max-vpcs`, `--no-max-vpcs`, `--max-public-ips`, `--no-max-public-ips`, `--max-hosted-zones`, `--no-max-hosted-zones`, `--max-record-sets`, `--no-max-record-sets` | Unsets `--max-vpcs`; the API's default applies. |
| `--max-public-ips <MAX_PUBLIC_IPS>` | one of `--max-instances`, `--no-max-instances`, `--max-vcpu`, `--no-max-vcpu`, `--max-volume-gib`, `--no-max-volume-gib`, `--max-vpcs`, `--no-max-vpcs`, `--max-public-ips`, `--no-max-public-ips`, `--max-hosted-zones`, `--no-max-hosted-zones`, `--max-record-sets`, `--no-max-record-sets` | The most floating IPs; unset means no budget. Left as it is when not given. `--no-max-public-ips` unsets it. |
| `--no-max-public-ips` | one of `--max-instances`, `--no-max-instances`, `--max-vcpu`, `--no-max-vcpu`, `--max-volume-gib`, `--no-max-volume-gib`, `--max-vpcs`, `--no-max-vpcs`, `--max-public-ips`, `--no-max-public-ips`, `--max-hosted-zones`, `--no-max-hosted-zones`, `--max-record-sets`, `--no-max-record-sets` | Unsets `--max-public-ips`; the API's default applies. |

Left as it is when not given. `--no-max-hosted-zones` unsets it. |

Left as it is when not given. `--no-max-record-sets` unsets it. |

## origin location

The platform's regions and zones, and which services each zone offers. A zonal list, such as a project's volumes, covers one zone: a client that wants every zone lists the zones here first. The same for every caller: any authenticated caller can read it, and no permission is needed.

Every `origin location` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host, `https://location.origincloudapis.eu`, the same in every region. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_LOCATION_ENDPOINT`. |

### get-region

Returns a region.

```sh
origin location get-region [OPTIONS] --region <REGION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--region <REGION>` | yes | The region to return, `regions/{region}`. Its id, or its whole name, `regions/{region}`. |

### list-regions

Lists every region that has a zone, in catalog order.

```sh
origin location list-regions [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### get-zone

Returns a zone.

```sh
origin location get-zone [OPTIONS] --zone <ZONE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--zone <ZONE>` | yes | The zone to return, `zones/{zone}`. Its id, or its whole name, `zones/{zone}`. |

### list-zones

Lists every zone, in catalog order. A zone offers a service when its `services` names it: those are the zones a client lists that service's zonal resources in.

```sh
origin location list-zones [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

## origin billing

Billing: billing accounts and the projects they pay for, payment methods, cost and usage, spend limits and the price list. Billing accounts and their spend limits are an organization's (`--organization`); a project's billing info names the account it is charged to. Access to billing is granted apart from access to projects: an organization's owner doesn't hold it by default.

Every `origin billing` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host, `https://billing.origincloudapis.eu`, the same in every region. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_BILLING_ENDPOINT`. |

### get-billing-account

Returns a billing account. Needs `admin.billing_account.get` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing get-billing-account [OPTIONS] --billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--billing-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The billing account to return. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/billingAccounts/{billing_account}`. |

### list-billing-accounts

Lists an organization's billing accounts, oldest first. Needs `admin.billing_account.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing list-billing-accounts [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most billing accounts to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### create-billing-account

Creates a billing account with its profile: `--display-name`, `--billing-address`, `--invoice-email` and `--contact-person` are required, and `--vat-id` too for a billing address outside Germany. The account has no payment method yet: until one is verified, the projects linked to it can't create billable resources. Creating it grants nobody a role: whoever can create billing accounts can use it. Needs `admin.billing_account.create` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing create-billing-account [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>` | yes | The name the console and spend-limit alerts show. Not empty. An organization's default account is called `default` until it is renamed. |
| `--billing-address <KEY=VALUE,...>` | no | The postal address invoices are issued to. Required to create an account; unset only on an organization's default account until its profile is set. As comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `street`, required: The street and house number. `city`, required: The city. `postal_code`, required: The postal code. `region_code`, required: The country, as the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of one of the countries ListBillingCountries lists, such as `DE`. A value with a comma in it goes through `--billing-address-json` too. |
| `--billing-address-json <JSON>` | no | As the API's JSON, an object whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. Instead of `--billing-address`. |
| `--invoice-email <INVOICE_EMAIL>` | no | Where invoices are sent. Required to create an account; empty only on an organization's default account until its profile is set. |
| `--vat-id <VAT_ID>` | no | The VAT identification number invoices name; empty for none. Required for a billing address outside Germany. |
| `--contact-person <CONTACT_PERSON>` | no | Who invoices are addressed to. Required to create an account; empty only on an organization's default account until its profile is set. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the billing account the first request created instead of creating a second one. One is generated when not given. |

### update-billing-account

Changes a billing account's `--display-name` or its profile. The profile fields named in `updateMask` are replaced and the others kept; once the update is applied, the account must have a whole profile (`--billing-address`, `--invoice-email`, `--contact-person`, and `--vat-id` for a billing address outside Germany), or the update is refused. Needs `admin.billing_account.update` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing update-billing-account [OPTIONS] --billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT> <--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>|--billing-address <KEY=VALUE,...>|--billing-address-json <JSON>|--no-billing-address|--invoice-email <INVOICE_EMAIL>|--vat-id <VAT_ID>|--contact-person <CONTACT_PERSON>>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--billing-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The billing account to change. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/billingAccounts/{billing_account}`. |
| `--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>` | one of `--display-name`, `--billing-address`, `--billing-address-json`, `--no-billing-address`, `--invoice-email`, `--vat-id`, `--contact-person` | The name the console and spend-limit alerts show. Not empty. An organization's default account is called `default` until it is renamed. Left as it is when not given. |
| `--billing-address <KEY=VALUE,...>` | one of `--display-name`, `--billing-address`, `--billing-address-json`, `--no-billing-address`, `--invoice-email`, `--vat-id`, `--contact-person` | The postal address invoices are issued to. Required to create an account; unset only on an organization's default account until its profile is set. As comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `street`, required: The street and house number. `city`, required: The city. `postal_code`, required: The postal code. `region_code`, required: The country, as the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of one of the countries ListBillingCountries lists, such as `DE`. A value with a comma in it goes through `--billing-address-json` too. It is replaced whole: a key not given is reset. `--no-billing-address` removes it. Left as it is when none of these is given. |
| `--billing-address-json <JSON>` | one of `--display-name`, `--billing-address`, `--billing-address-json`, `--no-billing-address`, `--invoice-email`, `--vat-id`, `--contact-person` | As the API's JSON, an object whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. Instead of `--billing-address`. It is replaced whole: a key not given is reset. `--no-billing-address` removes it. Left as it is when none of these is given. |
| `--no-billing-address` | one of `--display-name`, `--billing-address`, `--billing-address-json`, `--no-billing-address`, `--invoice-email`, `--vat-id`, `--contact-person` | Remove its billing address. |
| `--invoice-email <INVOICE_EMAIL>` | one of `--display-name`, `--billing-address`, `--billing-address-json`, `--no-billing-address`, `--invoice-email`, `--vat-id`, `--contact-person` | Where invoices are sent. Required to create an account; empty only on an organization's default account until its profile is set. Left as it is when not given. |
| `--vat-id <VAT_ID>` | one of `--display-name`, `--billing-address`, `--billing-address-json`, `--no-billing-address`, `--invoice-email`, `--vat-id`, `--contact-person` | The VAT identification number invoices name; empty for none. Required for a billing address outside Germany. Left as it is when not given. |
| `--contact-person <CONTACT_PERSON>` | one of `--display-name`, `--billing-address`, `--billing-address-json`, `--no-billing-address`, `--invoice-email`, `--vat-id`, `--contact-person` | Who invoices are addressed to. Required to create an account; empty only on an organization's default account until its profile is set. Left as it is when not given. |

### delete-billing-account

Deletes a billing account. Refused as a `CONFLICT` for the organization's default billing account, while a project is linked to the account (link it to another account first), and while the account has a spend limit (remove it first). Needs `admin.billing_account.delete` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing delete-billing-account [OPTIONS] --billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--billing-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The billing account to delete. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/billingAccounts/{billing_account}`. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### start-payment-method-setup

Starts adding a payment method to a billing account, and returns the payment provider's page to open in a browser: the payment details are entered there and never pass through this API. Once that page is done, call ConfirmPaymentMethodSetup. Starting again replaces a setup that wasn't confirmed. Refused as `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an account whose `payment_method.state` is `NOT_REQUIRED`. Needs `admin.billing_account.update` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing start-payment-method-setup [OPTIONS] --billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--billing-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The billing account to add a payment method to. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/billingAccounts/{billing_account}`. |

### confirm-payment-method-setup

Completes the setup StartPaymentMethodSetup started, once its page is done: the payment provider is asked whether it finished, and only a finished setup is recorded. The account's `paymentMethod` is then `VERIFIED`, replacing any earlier one, and its projects can create billable resources. An unfinished or abandoned setup is refused as `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and changes nothing: finish the page, or start again. So is an account with no setup started, which includes a repeat of a confirmation that succeeded: read the account to see whether it did. Needs `admin.billing_account.update` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing confirm-payment-method-setup [OPTIONS] --billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--billing-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The billing account whose setup to complete. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/billingAccounts/{billing_account}`. |

### get-project-billing-info

Returns which billing account pays for a project. Needs `admin.project.get` on the project.

```sh
origin billing get-project-billing-info [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | yes | The billing info to return, `projects/{project}/billingInfo`. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/billingInfo`. |

### update-project-billing-info

Links a project to another billing account of its organization, which pays for its usage from then on; what it used before stays charged to the account it was linked to then. A project is always linked to one account, so there is nothing to unlink. Needs `admin.project.attach` on the project, which is separate from access to billing accounts.

```sh
origin billing update-project-billing-info [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT> <--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--billing-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--project <PROJECT>` | yes | The project billing info to change. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/billingInfo`. |
| `--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The billing account that pays for the project's usage, one of its organization's. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/billingAccounts/{billing_account}`. Left as it is when not given. |

### list-project-billing-info

Lists the projects a billing account pays for, oldest first. Needs `admin.billing_account.get` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing list-project-billing-info [OPTIONS] --billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--billing-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The billing account whose projects to list. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/billingAccounts/{billing_account}`. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most projects to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### get-billing-country

Returns a country a billing address may be in.

```sh
origin billing get-billing-country [OPTIONS] --billing-country <BILLING_COUNTRY>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--billing-country <BILLING_COUNTRY>` | yes | The country to return, `billingCountries/{code}`, such as `billingCountries/DE`. Its id, or its whole name, `billingCountries/{billing_country}`. |

### list-billing-countries

Lists the countries a billing address may be in, in the order a form shows them, and whether each needs a VAT id.

```sh
origin billing list-billing-countries [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most countries to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### query-project-cost

Returns a project's cost in a period, by service and product, in hourly or daily buckets. Needs `admin.usage.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing query-project-cost [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT> --start-time <TIME> --end-time <TIME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | yes | The project, `projects/{project}`. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}`. |
| `--start-time <TIME>` | yes | The period's start, included. As RFC 3339, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`. |
| `--end-time <TIME>` | yes | The period's end, left out; after `--start-time`. As RFC 3339, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`. |
| `--granularity <GRANULARITY>` | no | How finely to bucket the cost; daily when unset. Possible values: `HOURLY`, `DAILY`. |

### query-organization-cost

Returns an organization's cost in a period: every project's together, by service and product, and each project's on its own. Needs `admin.usage.list` on the organization, which reads every project's cost in it.

```sh
origin billing query-organization-cost [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --start-time <TIME> --end-time <TIME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization, `organizations/{organization}`. Its id, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}`. |
| `--start-time <TIME>` | yes | The period's start, included. As RFC 3339, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`. |
| `--end-time <TIME>` | yes | The period's end, left out; after `--start-time`. As RFC 3339, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`. |
| `--granularity <GRANULARITY>` | no | How finely to bucket the cost; daily when unset. Possible values: `HOURLY`, `DAILY`. |

### query-billing-account-cost

Returns what was charged to a billing account in a period, by service and product. A project's cost is charged to the account it was linked to when the usage was recorded, so moving a project moves only its later cost. Its spend limit compares the calendar month's total with `limit`. Needs `admin.spend_limit.get` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing query-billing-account-cost [OPTIONS] --billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT> --start-time <TIME> --end-time <TIME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--billing-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The billing account. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/billingAccounts/{billing_account}`. |
| `--start-time <TIME>` | yes | The period's start, included. As RFC 3339, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`. |
| `--end-time <TIME>` | yes | The period's end, left out; after `--start-time`. As RFC 3339, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`. |
| `--granularity <GRANULARITY>` | no | How finely to bucket the cost; daily when unset. Possible values: `HOURLY`, `DAILY`. |

### query-project-usage

Lists a project's metered usage records that overlap a period, the input its cost is priced from, oldest first. Needs `admin.usage.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing query-project-usage [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT> --start-time <TIME> --end-time <TIME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | yes | The project, `projects/{project}`. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}`. |
| `--start-time <TIME>` | yes | The period's start: records that end after it are listed. As RFC 3339, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`. |
| `--end-time <TIME>` | yes | The period's end: records that start before it are listed; after `--start-time`. As RFC 3339, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most records to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### get-price-list

Returns the prices in effect now. The answer carries an `ETag`; a request that sends it back in `If-None-Match` is answered `304 Not Modified`, without a body, while the list is unchanged.

```sh
origin billing get-price-list [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### get-spend-limit

Returns a billing account's spend limit; one that has none has no `limit`. Needs `admin.spend_limit.get` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing get-spend-limit [OPTIONS] --billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--billing-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The spend limit to return. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/billingAccounts/{billing_account}/spendLimit`. |

### update-spend-limit

Sets or removes a billing account's spend limit. The fields named in `updateMask` are replaced and the others kept. A spend limit left without a `--limit` is removed, with its thresholds and recipients. Needs `admin.spend_limit.update` on the organization.

```sh
origin billing update-spend-limit [OPTIONS] --billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT> <--limit <LIMIT>|--no-limit|--alert-thresholds-percent <ALERT_THRESHOLDS_PERCENT>|--no-alert-thresholds-percent|--notification-email <NOTIFICATION_EMAIL>|--no-notification-emails>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--billing-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--billing-account <BILLING_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The spend limit to change. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/billingAccounts/{billing_account}/spendLimit`. |
| `--limit <LIMIT>` | one of `--limit`, `--no-limit`, `--alert-thresholds-percent`, `--no-alert-thresholds-percent`, `--notification-email`, `--no-notification-emails` | The amount per calendar month in EUR, before VAT, as a decimal string such as `500.00`; more than zero. Unset means no spend limit. Left as it is when not given. `--no-limit` unsets it. |
| `--no-limit` | one of `--limit`, `--no-limit`, `--alert-thresholds-percent`, `--no-alert-thresholds-percent`, `--notification-email`, `--no-notification-emails` | Unsets `--limit`; the API's default applies. |
| `--alert-thresholds-percent <ALERT_THRESHOLDS_PERCENT>` | one of `--limit`, `--no-limit`, `--alert-thresholds-percent`, `--no-alert-thresholds-percent`, `--notification-email`, `--no-notification-emails` | The percentages of `--limit` whose crossing emails an alert, such as `80` and `100`; each from 1 to 32767, so a threshold can lie beyond the limit. Empty while there is no `--limit`. Repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-alert-thresholds-percent` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-alert-thresholds-percent` | one of `--limit`, `--no-limit`, `--alert-thresholds-percent`, `--no-alert-thresholds-percent`, `--notification-email`, `--no-notification-emails` | Remove all of its alert thresholds percent. |
| `--notification-email <NOTIFICATION_EMAIL>` | one of `--limit`, `--no-limit`, `--alert-thresholds-percent`, `--no-alert-thresholds-percent`, `--notification-email`, `--no-notification-emails` | Where alerts are sent. Empty while there is no `--limit`, and an alert with no recipient is sent to nobody. Repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-notification-emails` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-notification-emails` | one of `--limit`, `--no-limit`, `--alert-thresholds-percent`, `--no-alert-thresholds-percent`, `--notification-email`, `--no-notification-emails` | Remove all of its notification emails. |

## origin support

Support: cases, each a conversation with Origin Cloud support about a question or a problem, and their messages. Cases are an organization's (`--organization`) and may name one of its projects. Every notification about a case goes to the contact email given when it was opened.

Every `origin support` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host, `https://support.origincloudapis.eu`, the same in every region. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_SUPPORT_ENDPOINT`. |

### get-case

Returns a case. Needs `admin.support_case.get` on the organization.

```sh
origin support get-case [OPTIONS] --case <CASE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--case` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--case <CASE>` | yes | The case to return. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/cases/{case}`. |

### list-cases

Lists an organization's cases, newest first. Needs `admin.support_case.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin support list-cases [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most cases to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### create-case

Opens a case, `OPEN`. Needs `admin.support_case.create` on the organization.

```sh
origin support create-case [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --subject <SUBJECT> --description <DESCRIPTION> --contact-email <CONTACT_EMAIL>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project the case is about, `projects/{project}`, one of the organization's. Empty for a case about the organization as a whole. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}`. |
| `--subject <SUBJECT>` | yes | A one-line summary. Not empty. |
| `--description <DESCRIPTION>` | yes | What the case is about, in full. Not empty. |
| `--contact-email <CONTACT_EMAIL>` | yes | The email address every notification about the case is sent to, for as long as the case exists: when support replies, and when its state changes. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the case the first request opened instead of opening a second one. One is generated when not given. |

### close-case

Closes a case: its `state` becomes `CLOSED`, and its contact email is notified. Closing a closed case succeeds and changes nothing. Needs `admin.support_case.update` on the organization.

```sh
origin support close-case [OPTIONS] --case <CASE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--case` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--case <CASE>` | yes | The case to close. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/cases/{case}`. |

### reopen-case

Opens a resolved or closed case again: its `state` becomes `OPEN`, and its contact email is notified. Reopening a case that is `OPEN` or `IN_PROGRESS` succeeds and changes nothing. Needs `admin.support_case.update` on the organization.

```sh
origin support reopen-case [OPTIONS] --case <CASE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--case` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--case <CASE>` | yes | The case to open again. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/cases/{case}`. |

### get-case-message

Returns one message of a case. Needs `admin.support_case.get` on the organization.

```sh
origin support get-case-message [OPTIONS] --message <MESSAGE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--message` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--case <CASE>` | no | The `{case}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--message` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--message <MESSAGE>` | yes | The message to return. Its id, completed with `--organization` and `--case`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/cases/{case}/messages/{message}`. |

### list-case-messages

Lists a case's messages, oldest first. Needs `admin.support_case.get` on the organization.

```sh
origin support list-case-messages [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --case <CASE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--case <CASE>` | yes | The `{case}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most messages to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### create-case-message

Adds a message to a case's conversation. The case's contact email is notified unless the message's author opened the case, so nobody is emailed their own messages. Needs `admin.support_case.create` on the organization.

```sh
origin support create-case-message [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --case <CASE> --body <BODY>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--case <CASE>` | yes | The `{case}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--body <BODY>` | yes | The message's text. Not empty. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the message the first request added instead of adding a second one. One is generated when not given. |

## origin mcp

Serve Origin Cloud's API to an AI agent over MCP, and add it to coding agents.

### serve

Serve Origin Cloud's API to an AI agent, as an MCP server on standard input and output. An MCP client, such as an AI coding assistant, starts it as a local server: `origin mcp serve`. It has a tool per method of the API, in a toolset per service, and calls them as this profile: with its login, or the credentials in ORIGINCLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN, or ORIGINCLOUD_CLIENT_ID and ORIGINCLOUD_CLIENT_SECRET, in the region the commands use (ORIGINCLOUD_REGION, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone), and with each service's endpoint variable, such as ORIGINCLOUD_PVS_ENDPOINT. The tool `current_context` tells the agent the profile's `default-project` and `default-zone`, and that region. The tools that delete something, or change it for good, are marked destructive for the client to confirm: they don't ask for `--yes`. `--read-only` leaves out every tool that changes anything.

```sh
origin mcp serve [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--toolsets <TOOLSET>` | no | The toolsets to expose, by service; every one when not given. Possible values: `billing`, `compute`, `dns`, `iam`, `location`, `network`, `observability`, `pvs`, `resourcemanager`, `support`. |
| `--read-only` | no | Expose only the tools that change nothing: reads, and waiting for operations. |

### install

Add `origin mcp serve` to a coding agent's MCP servers. Adds an entry, named `origincloud` unless `--name` says otherwise, that starts `origin mcp serve` with `--toolsets` and `--read-only`, and with `--config` when it was given (`origin --config FILE mcp install`). Where the agent has a command for this, such as `claude mcp add`, and it is on PATH, it runs that; otherwise it edits the agent's file, keeping everything else in it, comments included where the format has them, after copying it to `FILE.origin.bak`. Running it again updates the entry; a file that doesn't parse, or an entry of that name that doesn't start `origin mcp serve`, is left as it is. The entry holds no credentials: `origin mcp serve` uses the login and the profile, as the other commands do, so a project's file can be committed. On a terminal, without `--agent`, it offers the agents it finds on this machine.

```sh
origin mcp install [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent <AGENT>` | no | The coding agents, comma-separated; on a terminal without it, those found on this machine are offered. Possible values: - claude-code: Claude Code - codex: OpenAI Codex - cursor: Cursor - gemini-cli: Gemini CLI - github-copilot: GitHub Copilot (VS Code, Copilot CLI) - claude-desktop: Claude Desktop. |
| `--scope <SCOPE>` | no | `user`, the agent's own configuration, for every project; or `project`, the project in the current directory, in a file that is usually committed with it. Possible values: - user: Every project of this user, in the agent's own configuration - project: The project in the current directory, in a file beside its code. Default: `user`. |
| `--name <NAME>` | no | The name of the entry. Default: `origincloud`. |
| `--toolsets <TOOLSET>` | no | The toolsets to expose, by service; every one when not given. Possible values: `billing`, `compute`, `dns`, `iam`, `location`, `network`, `observability`, `pvs`, `resourcemanager`, `support`. |
| `--read-only` | no | Expose only the tools that change nothing: reads, and waiting for operations. |
| `--absolute-path` | no | Name the `origin` binary by its absolute path rather than as `origin`, for an agent that doesn't start it with the PATH of your shell. The agents started from a desktop launcher, such as Claude Desktop, always get it. |
| `--print` | no | Print the entry, as the agent's file would hold it, and change nothing. Without `--agent`, in the `mcpServers` form most agents read. |

### uninstall

Remove `origin mcp serve` from a coding agent's MCP servers. Removes the entry `origin mcp install` added, by its name, and nothing else, with the agent's command or by editing its file as `install` does. An entry of that name that doesn't start `origin mcp serve` is left as it is.

```sh
origin mcp uninstall [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent <AGENT>` | no | The coding agents, comma-separated; on a terminal without it, those found on this machine are offered. Possible values: - claude-code: Claude Code - codex: OpenAI Codex - cursor: Cursor - gemini-cli: Gemini CLI - github-copilot: GitHub Copilot (VS Code, Copilot CLI) - claude-desktop: Claude Desktop. |
| `--scope <SCOPE>` | no | `user`, the agent's own configuration, for every project; or `project`, the project in the current directory, in a file that is usually committed with it. Possible values: - user: Every project of this user, in the agent's own configuration - project: The project in the current directory, in a file beside its code. Default: `user`. |
| `--name <NAME>` | no | The name of the entry. Default: `origincloud`. |
